title.narrative: Promoting an improved understanding of the critical threat that explosive ordnance presents to affected people in Syria through surveys, clearance and risk education

description.narrative: The recent political changes in Syria offer an opportunity for HMA actors,previously operating in separate zones of control, to collaborate&coordinate for an improved response.Many areas, previously inaccessible,can now be surveyed for Explosive Ordnance(EO)contamination.This project coordinates a survey and EOD response across eleven Syrian governorates to build a comprehensive baseline of EO contamination across Syria&raising awareness among affected populations&humanitarians.By assessing the extent of the threat&addressing the most imminent of these risks,the project aims to ensure safe aid delivery,access to services, and restoration of livelihoods in affected areas. EO contamination endangers humanitarian workers&the people they serve. Considering the changes in the Syria context, UNMAS will expand its role as Mine Action AoR coordinator to effectively oversee,advise&coordinate the growing number of HMA actors operating across Syria.Objectives and strategic approach The core component of the project is the implementation of systematic EO surveys to gather&record data pertaining to the EO threat,resulting in a holistic picture of the known EO threat situation in Syria which would drive informed decision making,prioritisation&the coordination of future clearance,risk education&victim assistance activities. The goal of the project will be to protect populations residing in and transitioning through potential contaminated areas from EO risks, through raising awareness of and addressing the most imminent threats, enabling them to safely access humanitarian aid&essential services&facilitating a better understanding of the scale and presence of the threat.Key activitiesSurvey activities form the cornerstone of the project, playing a critical role in enabling communities to regain access to essential services&livelihood opportunities, whilst ensuring that humanitarian actors can operate safely in affected areas.To implement the survey initiatives,UNMAS,through mine action IPs,will deploy Non-Technical Survey(NTS),Technical Survey(TS),EO Disposal(EOD) and EO Risk Education(EORE)teams.Throughout the project duration,UNMAS,will coordinate, monitor&quality assure(QA)IP operations to ensure high-quality data collection through safe survey&clearance operations whilst actively engaging with partners in providing technical advice&guidance,promoting best practices amongst HMA operators.Data collected during these activities will be systematically analyzed &managed using the Information Management System for Mine Action(IMSMA)for promulgation to humanitarian&development partners, I/NGOs and government ministries.As part of this project UNMAS will also deploy specialized EORE teams to deliver risk education to affected communities,building on the success of a pilot initiative under a previous project.The program will recruit&train survivors of EO incidents& PwD to serve as EORE facilitators.This initiative has proven to be highly impactful,delivering powerful,relatable messages on EO risks while fostering resilience&inclusion within communities. ConclusionUNMAS is committed to addressing the escalating risks posed by EO contamination in Syria.By collaborating with UN agencies,NGOs,and other partners,UNMAS aims to enhance efforts to map the scale&scope of the EO contamination,addressing critical gaps in the broader humanitarian response.Through targeted survey activities, clearance operations & EORE initiatives, UNMAS will focus on specific areas that have previously lacked coordinated mine action,providing essential support to vulnerable communities&humanitarian personnel.This comprehensive approach not only mitigates the immediate risks of EO but also safeguards humanitarian operations&supports affected communities in reclaiming their lives&livelihoods. By integrating these efforts into the broader humanitarian&early recovery framework, the project will contribute meaningfully to fostering safer, more resilient communities across Syria.
